name: Ikkesh
overview: Ikkesh is a male biblical figure known primarily as the father of Ira, who was one of King David's mighty men. There is no record of his tribal affiliation or additional personal details beyond this familial connection. His mention is brief but notable within the context of David’s elite warriors.
namesAndTitles: The name Ikkesh is a proper name of Hebrew origin meaning 'crooked' or 'perverted.' This meaning is recorded in 2 Samuel 23:26 but does not indicate that the name was given by God. The name itself is unique and carries a distinct meaning within the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Ikkesh as the father of Ira, one of David’s mighty men, as noted in 2 Samuel 23:26. Beyond this paternal relationship, no other family connections are documented in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Ikkesh’s significance lies in his role as the father of Ira, who served as one of King David’s elite warriors, highlighting a family connection to the king’s military leadership. Although Ikkesh himself is not described as a warrior or leader, his mention establishes the lineage of a notable figure in David’s army. This brief reference underscores the importance of family ties in the narrative of David’s mighty men.
